answer: A staking kernel makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent locks a refundable deposit before trading, slashed if it double-votes or floods fake orders. Creating ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand deposits, which the attacker never recovers. Reputation grows like a garden — long-lived agents earn trust slowly through verified trades, while fresh accounts start near zero, so a swarm cannot instantly outvote honest agents. A prism of independent attestors checks work, uptime and payments separately, so one forged credential cannot pass every check at once.
